title: Deploying Advanced Nuclear Reactor Technologies for National Security
summary: The order directs deployment pathways for advanced nuclear reactors serving national-security installations and other high-priority federal needs. It treats firm, resilient, high-density power as enabling infrastructure for mission systems, including energy-intensive computing.
key_findings: Advanced reactors are framed as sources of resilient power for national-security missions.
Federal sites and acquisition authorities are positioned as early deployment environments.
Licensing, fuel, supply chains, safety, and project delivery remain core dependencies.
why_it_matters: It connects advanced nuclear deployment directly to the power demands of secure compute and critical installations.
ftfn_relevance: Creates follow-up lanes for site selection, licensing, fuel, procurement, construction, and operation.
evidence_limits: A deployment directive is not an operating reactor or completed project.
Timelines depend on licensing, fuel availability, suppliers, financing, construction, and local conditions.
